Strata v0.3 · deloitte
FoundationsBrandColourTypeScalesComponentsAccessibilityDivergenceLicence

A base extracted from Carbon, with every value shown its source.

Strata takes IBM Carbon's token architecture, layering model, spacing scale, motion curves and accessibility mechanisms largely intact, and diverges where the brief calls for something lighter — or where Carbon's own published guidance contradicts itself. Every token below carries the official Carbon value it came from, a link to the page it came from, and where they differ, the reason.

This page is not a description of the system. It is rendered from the system — the same tokens.json and strata.css the components consume. Nothing here can drift from what ships.

9 hue ramps · 10 grades · luminance-locked 65 semantic tokens 13 components 168 contrast checks, 0 failing axe-core: 0 violations Light + dark

Why this shape

You asked me to recommend the form and justify it. Four decisions, and what each one is defending against.

1 · Tokens are the deliverable, not the CSS

The artefact of record is tokens.json. CSS, the component styles and this page are all generated from it. The failure mode this prevents is real and Carbon demonstrates it: its published token table still prints $button-primary-hover as #0353e9 while @carbon/themes ships #0050e6, and prints $text-placeholder as Gray 40 while the code ships rgba(22,22,22,0.4). Two artefacts, two answers, and no way to know which is right without reading the source. One generator, one answer.

2 · A live style guide, not a spec document

A written spec cannot show you that a warning icon has 2.8:1 against its own background. This page renders every component from the shipped CSS and recomputes every contrast pair at build time. Design systems fail at the seams between the documentation and the artefact; removing the seam is cheaper than policing it.

3 · Framework-agnostic CSS custom properties

No React dependency in the base layer. The token and CSS layers outlive whatever renders them, and a React, Vue or Web Components binding can sit on top without forking the values. This mirrors Carbon's own structure — @carbon/colors, @carbon/type and @carbon/layout are framework-free by design — and it is why Carbon survived its own v10→v11 migration.

4 · Semantic tier is the contract

Components reference --st-layer-01, never --st-neutral-10. That single rule is what makes light/dark a data change rather than a code change, and it is the reason the whole palette can be re-hued without touching a component file. Carbon states it as: tokens are universal, roles never change between themes, only values do.

What was adopted wholesale

The 8px mini-unit spacing scale (all 13 steps). The 16-column 2x Grid and its five breakpoints. The productive motion curves and durations. The layering model, including the off-by-one field rule — a field placed on layer-02 uses field-03, but borders pair with their own number. The two-tone focus ring, drawn inset at outline-offset: -2px. The group-role-state-index token grammar. The interaction-state arithmetic: hover is a half step, selected one step, active two steps. Warning does not recolour a field border. Placeholder never replaces a label. Tags are not navigation. Toggles are only for instantly-applied settings. These are the parts of Carbon that are genuinely hard-won, and there is no reason to re-derive them.

Where it diverges, and the three reasons

Lighter, per your brief

Radius scale introduced and defaulted to 6px on controls. Chroma capped at roughly half Carbon's peak. Body text drops from 17.4:1 to 14.2:1. Scrims and shadows tinted with the neutral hue instead of pure black. Default body size 16px, not 14px.

Carbon contradicts itself

$text-placeholder fails 4.5:1 in both of its two conflicting official values. $support-warning is held constant across all four themes, breaking the theme contract, and fails 1.4.11 against its own notification background. Carbon requires 44px touch targets for icons but ships a 40px default field. The date picker field is set in the mono type token for no published reason. @carbon/themes ships two different values for $button-primary-hover from its own SCSS and JS builds.

Carbon leaves a gap

prefers-reduced-motion handled per-component in 12 SCSS files, with no token and no requirement — so coverage is partial by construction. No sticky-header data table spec, though the React implementation supports it. No dropdown menu max-height. No range-start calendar cell state. No radius scale. Status backgrounds locked inside the Notification component by the component-token confinement rule.

Brand — Deloitte

The primary action colour is Deloitte Green 349 (#046A38), the dark green. Neutrals are Deloitte Cool Gray. Everything else in the system is unchanged — this page exists so the brand mapping is auditable rather than asserted.

The dark green was the right call

Deloitte Green #86BC25 measures 2.27:1 against white. It cannot carry text, an icon, or a control boundary under WCAG AA — which is the standard Deloitte's own accessibility statement commits to. It is a mark colour. Green 349 at 6.72:1 is the first green in the official ramp that can be an action colour, and grade 70 reproduces it to within ΔRGB 5.

The grey shift was already done

Deloitte Cool Gray 10 and 11 sit at OKLCH hue 255.5°. Strata's neutral was already 255.0°. --st-neutral-70 was #55595d against Cool Gray 11's #53565A — ΔRGB 4. The brief was satisfied before it was written; the config now says so explicitly rather than leaving it to coincidence.

Deloitte's green ramp is not one hue

It swings from 109° at the light end to 153° at the dark end — a Pantone set, not a computed ramp. A single-hue ladder can hit one end or the other. Anchoring on the dark end (the interactive colour) means #86BC25 has to be carried as a pinned literal, outside the ramp, restricted to mark use.

One divergence reversed itself

--st-support-info was moved off blue because Carbon's blue info collided with Carbon's blue primary action. With a green primary that objection evaporates and blue is free, so info returns to Carbon's value — now as Deloitte Blue 7690, ΔRGB 3. The divergence was contingent on the brand, not on Carbon being wrong.

Where each official Deloitte value lands

A computed palette cannot promise to reproduce a hand-authored Pantone set. The honest thing is to state the mapping and the error rather than claim a match. ΔRGB is Euclidean distance in sRGB — under 10 is indistinguishable side by side, under 25 is a rounding difference, above that is a different colour.

The collision worth arguing about

With a green brand, the primary action and success are one grade apart in the same hue — green.70 and green.60. They are kept apart by form, not colour: --st-support-success only ever renders as a toggle track, a status icon or a 3px banner rule, never as a filled action-shaped surface, and every status carries an icon under the never-colour-alone rule already in the system. The alternative — moving success to teal — breaks the strongest colour convention in UI to solve a collision the form language already resolves, and would push info off Deloitte Blue. Scroll to Notification and Toggle below and judge it directly. If it bites in testing it is one line in build/tokens.py.

Before you ship this

Deloitte Green is a registered trademark — USPTO Reg. 5959457, "the mark consists of a green dot (Pantone 368)", colour claimed as a feature of the mark, registered January 2020. Separately, Acorns Grow Inc. holds US Reg. 6176921 over Pantone 368 C as applied to the background of a software application. This system assumes you are building for or with Deloitte and are licensed to use the palette. If that assumption is wrong, this is not a design question.

Colour

Nine hue ramps of ten grades, plus black and white. Carbon hand-authors each hue, which is why it has to publish a lookup table telling you how many steps apart two colours must be to reach a given contrast ratio. Strata pins every grade to a fixed relative luminance and solves for OKLCH lightness, so grade 60 has the same contrast behaviour in every hue and the lookup table becomes exact rather than advisory.

Grade → contrast against white, in every hue: 10 → 1.08:1 · 20 → 1.28:1 · 30 → 1.62:1 · 40 → 2.15:1 · 50 → 3.05:1 (the 1.4.11 non-text floor) · 60 → 5.00:1 (the 1.4.3 text floor, with headroom) · 70 → 7.1:1 · 80 → 10.6:1 · 90 → 14.2:1 · 100 → 17.4:1. Swapping a hue cannot silently break a contrast guarantee, because the guarantee lives in the ladder rather than in the individual value.

Changed Carbon: IBM Design Language palette — 12 families, 10 grades each, hand-authored, plus a separate hand-authored "hover spectrum" of half-steps. Blue 60 #0f62fe at OKLCH chroma ≈ 0.25. Strata caps chroma at 0.166 at grade 60 (red and magenta excepted — a hesitant error colour is a usability bug) and computes the hover half-step from the ladder instead of maintaining a second table. The IBM hex values are Apache-2.0 and could legally be copied verbatim; they are not, because IBM Blue plus a Plex-like face plus IBM densities is a trade-dress exposure that the software licence does not cover. /elements/color/overview/

Changed Carbon: IBM Plex Sans / Serif / Mono. Scale formula Yn = Yn-1 + (floor((n-2)/4)+1)·2 from 12px. Type sets split productive (-01, fixed) and expressive (-02, fluid). The scale formula is kept exactly. The face changes for licensing reasons: IBM Plex is SIL OFL-1.1 with "Plex" as a Reserved Font Name, so a modified cut must be renamed and the font files cannot be relicensed under Apache-2.0 alongside the rest of a fork — the most commonly botched part of forking Carbon. Strata also drops Carbon's fluid type entirely for now: eleven tokens that interpolate across five breakpoints is a large surface for a base layer, and Carbon itself concedes the productive/expressive split "is no longer neatly divided". /elements/typography/type-sets/

Space, size, radius, elevation, motion

The spacing scale is Carbon's, untouched. Radius is new. Elevation is rebuilt.

AdoptedCarbon: spacing-01..13 = 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 160px. Carbon's own wording: the scale uses 'multiples of two, four, and eight'. Note the 8px mini unit is a 2x GRID concept, not the basis of the spacing scale — 2, 4 and 12 are not multiples of 8. The two are complementary, not the same rule.Adopted wholesale, all 13 values. This is the single strongest part of Carbon: a 13-step scale on multiples of 2/4/8 covers everything from icon insets to page gutters without anyone reaching for an arbitrary number./elements/spacing/overview/

Control sizes

xs24px
sm32px
md40px
lg48px
xl64px
ChangedCarbon: Carbon control heights: xs 24, sm 32, md 40, lg 48, xl 64, 2xl 80. Default for product UI is large-productive (48) for buttons, medium (40) for fields.The scale is kept 1:1 so anything ported from Carbon maps without arithmetic. What changes is the DEFAULT: Strata defaults every interactive control to lg (48px), fields included. Carbon's own accessibility guidance requires 'all touch targets for interactive icons need to be 44px or larger' (/elements/icons/usage/) yet its default field is 40px -- an internal inconsistency. Defaulting to 48 clears the 44px floor for every control, not just icons. 32px remains available for data-dense surfaces. xs (24) is carried because Carbon carries it and the resolution map cites it for table row height -- but it is a ROW height only. It is below the 44px touch floor and must never size an interactive control./components/button/usage/

Radius

none0px
xs2px
sm4px
md6px
lg8px
xl10px

Plus radius-full (9999px) for pills. Component defaults: controls 6px, surfaces 8px, checkbox 2px, tags and toggles pill.

AddedCarbon: Carbon has no radius scale, no radius token in @carbon/layout or @carbon/themes, and no published square-corner rule or rationale anywhere on the site. Four component pages do publish a radius — Tag 16px, Content switcher 4px, Code snippet 2px, Popover 2px — while 23 component SCSS files set border-radius in shipped code (button, checkbox, toggle, tile, tooltip, slider, list-box...).Worth being precise, because 'Carbon is square-cornered' is folklore. It is not a documented rule. What Carbon actually has is radius applied ad hoc in 23 files with only four values ever documented — which is the definition of a scale that should exist and doesn't. Strata makes it explicit and moves the control default from 0 to 6px. Because it is a token, reverting the whole system to square is a one-line change./components/popover/style/

Elevation

00 · none
01 · hover lift
02 · menus, popovers
03 · modals
ChangedCarbon: One shadow mixin: `box-shadow: 0 2px 6px $shadow` where $shadow is black @30% (light themes) / @80% (dark). Plus a hardcoded 0 2px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.2) on Popover. Carbon states: 'Tiles reside on the same plane as the page background layer and do not have elevation... Do not add a drop shadow to tiles.'Strata keeps the layering model as the primary depth mechanism for in-flow surfaces -- that part of Carbon is excellent and is why Carbon reads calm. But a single 30%-black shadow is blunt: it is too heavy for a dropdown and too weak for a modal, which is exactly why Carbon had to hardcode a different one on Popover. Strata publishes three levels, all two-layer (tight contact shadow + diffuse ambient) and all tinted with the neutral hue rather than pure black, which is the single biggest contributor to a 'softer' surface read./components/tile/usage/

Added: a global prefers-reduced-motion: reduce rule that collapses every transition to 1ms. Carbon's position here is partial rather than absent: its Motion overview gives advisory prose ("Consider simplified or reduced motion designs… make sure there is always a way to communicate similar messages statically") and 12 component SCSS files implement the media query individually — but there is no motion opt-out token and no normative requirement, so whether a given component respects the preference depends on whether someone remembered. One global rule makes coverage total and removes the per-component decision.

Icons

Grid32 x 32px master grid
Padding2px on all four sides (28 x 28px live area)
Stroke2px, uniform
Corner Radius2px, increased in multiples of two where needed
Angles45 degrees primary; 15-degree increments elsewhere
Touch Target44px minimum, padded up in CSS where the glyph is smaller
Coloursolid and monochromatic; must pass 4.5:1, same as type
Alignmentcentre-aligned to adjacent text, never baseline-aligned

Artboard sizes: sm 16px · md 20px · lg 24px · xl 32px. No asset set ships with this base — the guide uses eleven placeholder glyphs.

AdoptedCarbon: Verbatim from IBM Design Language: 'IBM icons are drawn on a pixel-based grid of 32px x 32px'; 'The grid contains 2px padding'; 'Use a 2px stroke for all icons to maintain uniformity'; 'Use a consistent corner radius of 2px for rounded shapes'; 'Use 45 degree angles for even anti-aliasing. Use increments of 15 degrees whenever possible'. Artboard sizes 16/20/24/32 come from /elements/icons/usage/. @carbon/icons v11.85.0 ships 2,734 icons (2,711 non-deprecated) across 2,828 SVG assets, licensed Apache-2.0 with no icon-specific restriction.Construction rules adopted wholesale — they are well-reasoned and independently verifiable. No asset set is shipped here; the guide uses eleven placeholder glyphs. One caveat if you take Carbon's icons directly: the library contains several hundred logo--* and ibm-* marks, and Apache-2.0 SS6 licenses the files but grants no rights in the trademarks they depict.www.ibm.com/design/language/iconography/ui-icons/design

Aspect ratios

1:1 2:1 1:2 3:2 2:3 4:3 3:4 16:9 9:16
AdoptedCarbon: The 2x Grid page publishes six ratios (1:1, 2:1, 2:3, 3:2, 4:3, 16:9) 'in either portrait or landscape'. The shipped code makes the inversions explicit: nine classes on the pattern .cds--aspect-ratio--{W}x{H} plus a required .cds--aspect-ratio base class, exposed as the overridable $aspect-ratios variable. Note this lives in scss/components/aspect-ratio/, not scss/utilities/.Nine ratios adopted verbatim, including the three portrait inversions the docs imply but do not enumerate./elements/2x-grid/overview/

Components

Thirteen components, live, driven entirely by the tokens above. Each carries its spec measured against the official Carbon style page it derives from. Try the dark toggle in the header — no component CSS changes, only the semantic layer re-resolves.

ChangedCarbon: seven sizes across two variants — button xs 24, sm 32, md 40, large-productive 48, large-expressive 48; full-bleed button xl 64, 2xl 80Same scale, default moved to 48 to clear the 44px touch floor. The two 48s and the full-bleed-only 64/80 are collapsed: a size scale with two entries at the same height is a naming artefact, not a size.
Padding16px both sides; label centred
ChangedCarbon: 16px left / 64px right on a button with NO icon. Buttons with icons, icon-only buttons and all ghost buttons are already 16/16. Carbon's stated basis: 'When we say "fixed," there is a fixed padding of 16px to the left and a 64px padding to the right of the button label. The button label determines the button's width.' Paired with the Do caption 'Do left-align the label in a button, even if the button is wide.'Narrower than it first looks — Carbon is already symmetric in four of five cases, so this changes one. Carbon does publish a rationale for the 16 (nothing within 16px of a border; >=16px between label and icon so adjacent icon buttons stay separable) but none for the 64. The result is a button whose visual centre of mass sits left of its geometric centre, which is why a separate left-align rule is needed to keep it consistent. Strata centres the label instead.

ChangedCarbon: border-bottom 1px $border-strong only; no side or top borderCarbon's underline-only field is the strongest single signal of its visual identity, and the hardest to defend. A field with no left, right or top edge does not read as a container, its click target is ambiguous, and adjacent fields in a row visually merge. Carbon then has to switch to a full 2px border on focus and on error — so the boxed form already exists in the system, it is just withheld from the resting state. A full 1px border makes the resting, focus and error states the same shape.

A hover lift on a clickable tile is a state change, not decoration, and it is the cheapest way to distinguish a clickable tile from a base one before the pointer commits.

Accessibility audit

Carbon targets WCAG 2.1 AA via the IBM Accessibility Checklist, and is careful to say it "strives to meet" rather than conforms. Strata inherits the target and adds a build-time check so the claim is testable.

348 programmatic checks — 316 enforced, 0 failing. Recomputed on every build from the emitted token values; an AA failure aborts the build rather than shipping. The remaining 32 are marked advisory: disabled states, which WCAG explicitly exempts, and decorative boundaries not required to identify a component. They are reported so the number is visible, not enforced — a table row divider that hit 3:1 would be a worse table.

Alpha tokens are genuinely composited. A token like --st-background-active is a wash at 40% opacity; checking its base colour instead of the composite over-reports contrast for every alpha token in the system. Adding the real source-over composite to this build immediately surfaced three failures that had been invisible — a dark-theme placeholder at 3.48:1, a dark secondary button label at 3.04:1, and a dark toggle handle at 2.16:1. All three are now fixed, and all three exist in Carbon at the corresponding tokens.

Mechanisms carried over from Carbon

The two-tone focus ring. 2px --st-focus at outline-offset: -2px, so the ring is drawn inside the element's box and cannot collide with an adjacent control in a dense layout. On filled surfaces where the ring colour and the fill are close, a --st-focus-inset ring sits just inside it; because focus-inset is the theme's opposite pole, the pair is guaranteed to contrast against any underlying colour. This is the single most transferable idea in Carbon's accessibility model.

prefers-contrast handling. Solid rings become dotted, lifted from Carbon's _focus-outline.scss.

Never colour alone. Every status carries an icon; the selected tab carries weight 600 as well as an underline; selected table rows carry a checkbox; selected tiles carry a border-width change. All four survive greyscale.

44px touch floor. Carbon publishes it for interactive icons and then ships a 40px default field. Strata defaults every control to 48px so the floor applies system-wide.

Mechanisms Carbon does not have

forced-colors / Windows High Contrast Mode. Carbon handles prefers-contrast and never addresses forced-colors, where the OS strips every background and shadow. Anything carrying meaning by fill alone — a primary button, a selected row, a status tag, a toggle track — simply disappears. Strata restates each of those in a channel HCM preserves: system-colour borders throughout, the Highlight / HighlightText pair for the primary action (the native OS convention for a default button), a doubled border for danger, GrayText for disabled, and Highlight outlines on selected rows and dates. Without this the five button variants collapse into one identical box.

Reduced motion, systematised. One global rule rather than 12 per-component implementations — see the motion section.

An enforced audit. The table above is recomputed at build time and a failure aborts the build. Carbon publishes contrast targets but ships several tokens that miss them.

Automated checks run against this page

axe-core 4.x: 0 violations in both themes, across the whole document including every live component demo. Getting there caught one real bug in this system — the calendar's out-of-month days were using --st-text-disabled at 1.83:1. They are selectable, so the disabled exemption does not apply; Carbon specifies $text-secondary there and had it right where this build had it wrong.

Rendering verified in Chromium 141 at 1x and 2x, in light and dark, and under emulated forced-colors: active, prefers-contrast: more and prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Not verified: Safari and Firefox were not executable in the build environment. In place of that, the stylesheet's feature surface was audited by hand — :focus-visible, negative outline-offset, logical properties, place-items, flex gap, :indeterminate and font-variant-numeric are all supported in Safari 15.4+ and Firefox 85+; appearance carries its -webkit- prefix; and the two modern features used anywhere (color-mix() and backdrop-filter) appear only in this page's own chrome, behind an @supports guard with a solid fallback. Nothing in strata.css itself requires a feature newer than Safari 15.4.

Divergence ledger

Everything that is not Carbon, in one place, with the argument attached. This is the document to review — adopting Carbon's decisions needs no defence, departing from them does.

Roughly 93 decisions adopted from Carbon unchanged, 73 deliberately diverged. Every row below is a decision someone can argue with — which is the point of writing them down.

AreaToken / propertyChangeCarbon saysWhy we diverge
Colour--st-background-activeChanged$background-active — Gray 50 @50% light / @40% darkCarbon's 50% active wash on light themes drops the underlying label to roughly 2.4:1 mid-press. 40% keeps the state legible for the whole duration of the interaction.
Colour--st-background-brandChanged$background-brand — Blue 60 #0f62fe in all four themesDeloitte Green 349 #046A38. Grade 70 reproduces it to within delta-RGB 5 in the light theme. NOT held constant across themes, which is where Carbon does hold it constant: a grade-70 fill on a grade-100 page measures 2.45:1 and barely reads as a surface at all. Dark drops to grade 60 for 3.48:1.
Colour--st-border-subtle-00Changed$border-subtle-00 — Gray 20 / Gray 80Lightened to the whisper hairline of the 20 Aug 2026 visual language (composites to ~#ececed on white). Separation is carried by the hairline plus the resting shadow, not tone.
Colour--st-border-subtle-01Changed$border-subtle-01 — Gray 30 / Gray 70One step lighter than Carbon's: grade 20/80 (the old subtle-00 values). Part of the same E-04 re-cut.
Colour--st-border-strong-01Changed$border-strong-01 — Gray 50 #8d8d8d in both light themesCarbon uses Gray 50 for border-strong on every light layer. Against layer-01 (#f4f4f4) that measures 3.02:1 — it passes 1.4.11, but by 0.02. Strata uses neutral-60, which measures 4.62:1 on layer-01 and 4.99:1 on the page background, so the guarantee survives a hue swap or a rounding change.
Colour--st-border-interactiveChanged$border-interactive — Blue 60 / Blue 50Moved to grade 70 rather than 60 so it sits with the primary action and opens a clear gap to $support-success at grade 60. 7.1:1 on the page background.
Colour--st-border-interactive-subtleAddedNo Carbon counterpart — Carbon's tertiary uses a full-strength $button-tertiary borderThe 20 Aug 2026 language draws tertiary as a white surface with a tinted hairline; grade 30 light / 70 dark keeps it recognisably interactive without competing with primary.
Colour--st-text-primaryChanged$text-primary — Gray 100 #161616 / Gray 10 #f4f4f4Carbon's light-theme body text is Gray 100 at 17.4:1 on white. That is far past AAA and is a large part of why Carbon reads hard-edged. neutral-90 gives 14.2:1 — still comfortably AAA, measurably softer. Note this is a deliberate reduction in contrast and is the one divergence to revisit if the product targets low-vision users or bright-sunlight field use.
Colour--st-text-placeholderChanged$text-placeholder — rgba(22,22,22,0.4) in shipped @carbon/styles; Gray 40 #a8a8a8 in the /elements/color/tokens/ table. The two official sources disagree.Both Carbon values fail 4.5:1 against their own field background (#f4f4f4): the composited rgba value measures 2.53:1, Gray 40 measures 2.16:1. Placeholder is text and WCAG 1.4.3 applies. neutral-60 gives 4.62:1 on field-01 in light; dark uses grade 40, because grade 50 measures only 3.48:1 against field-02 (a field nested on layer-01) — the composited contrast audit caught that, the eye would not have. Carbon's own rule that placeholder must never replace a persistent label is kept and enforced in the component CSS.
Colour--st-text-disabledChanged$text-disabled — text-primary @25%25% of Carbon's Gray 100 lands near 1.9:1. Disabled text is exempt from contrast minimums, but 'exempt' is not 'illegible'. 30% reads as clearly-off without becoming invisible.
Colour--st-text-errorChanged$text-error — Red 60 #da1e28 / Red 40Red 60 on a Gray 10 field measures ~4.3:1 in Carbon. Grade 70 clears 4.5:1 against every light surface in the system.
Colour--st-link-primaryChanged$link-primary — Blue 60 / Blue 40Green, matching the interactive colour — a system with two different 'this is clickable' hues teaches nothing. Grade 70 so a link still clears 4.5:1 on layer-01 and inside a filled table row, not only on white.
Colour--st-link-hoverChanged$link-primary-hover — Blue 70 / Blue 30Follows link-primary.
Colour--st-link-visitedChanged$link-visited — Purple 60 / Purple 40The one deliberately off-brand token in the system. Deloitte's palette has no purple, and visited-link needs a hue that carries no other meaning here — green is interactive, blue is informational, teal and orange are categorical, red and amber are status. Every Deloitte hue is spoken for. Substituting one would make 'visited' collide with a live signal, which is worse than an off-brand link. Drop visited styling entirely if that trade is unacceptable.
Colour--st-icon-disabledChanged$icon-disabled — icon-primary @25%Matched to text-disabled for the same reason.
Colour--st-icon-interactiveChanged$icon-interactive — Blue 60 / WhiteBrand green.
Colour--st-support-successChanged$support-success — Green 50 / Green 40Value unchanged, but the RELATIONSHIP changed and this is the one token to argue about. With a green brand, success and the primary action are now one grade apart in the same hue (green.60 vs green.70). They are kept apart by form, not by colour: support-success only ever renders as a toggle track, a status icon or a 3px banner rule, never as a filled action-shaped surface, and every status carries an icon under the never-colour-alone rule. The alternative — moving success to teal — breaks the strongest colour convention in UI (green = good) to solve a collision the form language already resolves, and would push info off Deloitte Blue. If user testing says otherwise it is one line: change this to teal.60 / teal.30 and move the tag palette with it.
Colour--st-support-warningChanged$support-warning — Yellow 30 #f1c21b in ALL FOUR themesTwo problems fixed at once. (1) Carbon holds Yellow 30 constant across light and dark, breaking the contract that every semantic token re-resolves per theme. (2) Yellow 30 measures ~1.6:1 on white, so a Carbon warning icon fails 1.4.11 against its own notification background — the status that most needs to be noticed is the one that disappears. Strata resolves per theme and drops to grade 60 in light, which measures 4.6:1 on the warning surface. It reads as ochre rather than school-bus yellow; that is the cost of making it visible.
Colour--st-support-error-subtleAddedComponent tokens $notification-error-background-color. Values not published on the docs page for dark themes.Promoted from a Notification-only component token to a core token. Status backgrounds are needed by banners, table cells, form sections and inline validation, not just the Notification component, and Carbon's component-token confinement rule ('should never be used for anything other than their own component') would otherwise force a duplicate.
Colour--st-support-success-subtleAddedas aboveas above
Colour--st-support-warning-subtleAddedas aboveas above
Colour--st-support-info-subtleAddedas aboveas above
Colour--st-interactiveChanged$interactive — Blue 60 / Blue 50Brand green.
Colour--st-button-primaryChanged$button-primary — Blue 60 in all themesDeloitte Green 349. Grade 70, not 60: the brand's dark green is a 7.1:1 colour, and it leaves grades 80 and 90 free for hover and active. A grade-60 green would have run out of room. The dark theme uses grade 60 instead: at grade 70 the button barely separates from the page (2.45:1), and the near-black $focus-inset ring inside it fell to 2.46:1 — the composited audit caught that, and it is a failure mode a blue primary never had because Carbon's Blue 60 is a lighter colour than Deloitte's dark green.
Colour--st-button-secondaryChanged$button-secondary — Gray 80 / Gray 60Dark theme drops a grade. Carbon's dark secondary button is Gray 60 with $text-on-color (white) on it, which measures about 3.5:1 — under 4.5:1 for a button label. Grade 70 gives 7.1:1 and leaves room for the hover to lighten without crossing the threshold.
Colour--st-button-secondary-hoverChanged$button-secondary-hover — Gray 80 hover / Gray 60 hoverFollows the base grade. Carbon's dark hover lightens toward Gray 50, where a white label falls to roughly 3.0:1 — the hover state is where the label becomes least readable, which is backwards.
Colour--st-button-disabledChanged$button-disabled — Gray 30 / Gray 50 @30%Gray 30 against a white page is a loud disabled state. Grade 20 recedes; the disabled label still reads at ~3.4:1 against it.
Colour--st-overlayChanged$overlay — Black @60% in all four themesTinted with the neutral hue instead of pure black, and lightened in light themes. Pure black scrims are the other half of why Carbon reads industrial.
Colour--st-highlightChanged$highlight — Blue 20 / Blue 90Brand green.
Colour--st-toggle-handleChanged$icon-on-color — White in every themeA white handle on Carbon's dark-theme $support-success (Green 40) measures about 2.2:1 — the handle, which is the only thing communicating the toggle's position, is the least visible part of it in dark mode. Strata inverts the handle with the theme: 5.0:1 and 4.7:1 in light, 6.6:1 and 4.7:1 in dark, on the on and off tracks respectively.
Type--st-type-labelChangedlabel-01 — 12px / 16px / 400 / 0.32pxThe caps micro-label of the T1 ramp: weight 500 and wider tracking because it renders uppercase (the class sets text-transform). One label style, not two — label-md retired with the ramp.
Type--st-type-body-smChangedlabel-01 — 12px / 16px / 400 / 0.32px (nearest)T1's small running text: 12px with a taller line and tighter tracking than a label, because it sets sentences, not tags.
Type--st-type-body-mdChangedbody-compact-01 14px / body-01 14px (nearest)THE body size. 13.5px is the T1 working-density body — denser than the previous 16px default (that divergence is hereby reversed), calmer than Carbon's 14 at these weights. Off-scale knowingly; the ramp is hand-tuned, not formula-derived.
Type--st-type-heading-smChangedheading-compact-01 — 14px / 18px / 600 / 0.16px (nearest)Body-size heading: inline heads, card titles, table headers. Same size as body-md — weight alone carries the emphasis, which is the T1 rule.
Type--st-type-heading-mdChangedheading-compact-02 — 16px / 22px / 600 / 0px (nearest)The section head. One size above body, weight-led, a whisper of negative tracking.
Type--st-type-displayChangedheading-04 — 28px / 36px / 400 / 0pxThe one display moment: page titles and stat figures. 600 not 300/400 — T1 was chosen over Carbon's light-display treatment by eye, on identical pages. Negative tracking per the large-text rule the old heading-lg established.
FoundationSizingChangedCarbon control heights: xs 24, sm 32, md 40, lg 48, xl 64, 2xl 80. Default for product UI is large-productive (48) for buttons, medium (40) for fields.The scale is kept 1:1 so anything ported from Carbon maps without arithmetic. What changes is the DEFAULT: Strata defaults every interactive control to lg (48px), fields included. Carbon's own accessibility guidance requires 'all touch targets for interactive icons need to be 44px or larger' (/elements/icons/usage/) yet its default field is 40px -- an internal inconsistency. Defaulting to 48 clears the 44px floor for every control, not just icons. 32px remains available for data-dense surfaces. xs (24) is carried because Carbon carries it and the resolution map cites it for table row height -- but it is a ROW height only. It is below the 44px touch floor and must never size an interactive control.
FoundationRadiusAddedCarbon has no radius scale, no radius token in @carbon/layout or @carbon/themes, and no published square-corner rule or rationale anywhere on the site. Four component pages do publish a radius — Tag 16px, Content switcher 4px, Code snippet 2px, Popover 2px — while 23 component SCSS files set border-radius in shipped code (button, checkbox, toggle, tile, tooltip, slider, list-box...).Worth being precise, because 'Carbon is square-cornered' is folklore. It is not a documented rule. What Carbon actually has is radius applied ad hoc in 23 files with only four values ever documented — which is the definition of a scale that should exist and doesn't. Strata makes it explicit and moves the control default from 0 to 6px. Because it is a token, reverting the whole system to square is a one-line change.
FoundationElevationChangedOne shadow mixin: `box-shadow: 0 2px 6px $shadow` where $shadow is black @30% (light themes) / @80% (dark). Plus a hardcoded 0 2px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.2) on Popover. Carbon states: 'Tiles reside on the same plane as the page background layer and do not have elevation... Do not add a drop shadow to tiles.'Strata keeps the layering model as the primary depth mechanism for in-flow surfaces -- that part of Carbon is excellent and is why Carbon reads calm. But a single 30%-black shadow is blunt: it is too heavy for a dropdown and too weak for a modal, which is exactly why Carbon had to hardcode a different one on Popover. Strata publishes three levels, all two-layer (tight contact shadow + diffuse ambient) and all tinted with the neutral hue rather than pure black, which is the single biggest contributor to a 'softer' surface read.
Componentbutton · HeightsChangedCarbon: seven sizes across two variants — button xs 24, sm 32, md 40, large-productive 48, large-expressive 48; full-bleed button xl 64, 2xl 80Same scale, default moved to 48 to clear the 44px touch floor. The two 48s and the full-bleed-only 64/80 are collapsed: a size scale with two entries at the same height is a naming artefact, not a size.
Componentbutton · PaddingChangedCarbon: 16px left / 64px right on a button with NO icon. Buttons with icons, icon-only buttons and all ghost buttons are already 16/16. Carbon's stated basis: 'When we say "fixed," there is a fixed padding of 16px to the left and a 64px padding to the right of the button label. The button label determines the button's width.' Paired with the Do caption 'Do left-align the label in a button, even if the button is wide.'Narrower than it first looks — Carbon is already symmetric in four of five cases, so this changes one. Carbon does publish a rationale for the 16 (nothing within 16px of a border; >=16px between label and icon so adjacent icon buttons stay separable) but none for the 64. The result is a button whose visual centre of mass sits left of its geometric centre, which is why a separate left-align rule is needed to keep it consistent. Strata centres the label instead.
Componentbutton · RadiusChangedCarbon: not published on the style page, and _button.scss sets no border-radiusSee the radius scale.
Componentbutton · IconChangedCarbon: 16x16 icon (20x20 expressive); 32px label-to-icon gap on filled buttons, 8px on ghostOne gap value. The 32px filled-button gap is a consequence of the 64px right pad, not an independent decision.
Componentbutton · FocusChangedCarbon: the style page publishes only colours ($focus border, $focus-inset inset) plus 'box-shadow: inset | 1px'. Shipped code is a 1px border that turns $focus, with box-shadow inset 1px $focus AND inset 2px in the button's own background colour — so the visible double ring is 1px+2px, not 2px+1px.Strata uses the generic 2px/-2px geometry from Carbon's own focus-outline mixin for every control including buttons, rather than button's bespoke 1px border-plus-two-shadows construction. Same two-tone mechanism, one implementation.
Componenttext-input · HeightsChangedCarbon: 32 / 40 (default) / 48Default moved to lg, as with buttons.
Componenttext-input · BorderChangedCarbon: border-bottom 1px $border-strong only; no side or top borderCarbon's underline-only field is the strongest single signal of its visual identity, and the hardest to defend. A field with no left, right or top edge does not read as a container, its click target is ambiguous, and adjacent fields in a row visually merge. Carbon then has to switch to a full 2px border on focus and on error — so the boxed form already exists in the system, it is just withheld from the resting state. A full 1px border makes the resting, focus and error states the same shape.
Componenttext-input · RadiusChangedNot publishedSee the radius scale.
Componenttext-input · Field stackChangedCarbon (forms pattern page, not the text-input style page): 'we recommend a 32px spacer between input fields' on dedicated pages, 'designers can revert to 24px or even 16px' in contained forms, and 'a 48px spacer between the last input and the button or button group'. The Form style page gives a partly different set again.One value instead of three. 32px at a 14px body was proportionate; at a 16px body with taller controls it over-separates.
Componentcheckbox · ControlChangedCarbon: 16x16px, 1px border. Radius is not published on the style page, but _checkbox.scss ships border-radius: 2px — the 2px is Carbon's own value, just undocumented.Size only: 18px to sit better against a 16px body line, and to narrow Carbon's own unexplained gap between its 16px checkbox and 20px radio. The 2px radius is adopted, not invented.
Componentcheckbox · Item gapChangedCarbon: checkbox items 4px apart, radio items 8px apartCarbon states both values on its two style pages. Unified at 8px.
Componentcheckbox · LabelChangedCarbon: $body-compact-01, padding-left 8px ($spacing-03)Body token only; spacing identical.
Componentradio · ControlChangedCarbon: 20x20px control, 8px dotMatched to the checkbox at 18px.
Componentselect · Right paddingChangedCarbon: 48px ($spacing-09) on both the dropdown and select structure tables — though _dropdown.scss actually ships 42px, so Carbon's own code disagrees with its published value40px clears a 16px chevron with 16px of inset at 48px tall, and it is one value rather than two.
Componentselect · MenuChangedCarbon: $layer surface, box-shadow 0 2px 6px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.2), border-radius 0. A scroll threshold IS published: 'We recommend starting a scroll at the sixth option in the menu list' while 'showing 50% of the last option's container height to indicate there is more to see'. Shipped as max-block-size 220px (40px item x 5.5).Carbon's rule restated at Strata's row height — 320px is six 48px rows, the same intent as Carbon's 220px at 40px rows. Strata publishes the px value as well as the rule, so it can be a token.
Componentdate-picker · Field textChangedCarbon: $code-02 (!). Every other Carbon field uses $body-compact-01Carbon's date field is the only one set in the mono type token. There is no published rationale; the plausible one is tabular figure alignment, which is better served by font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on the normal face. Strata does that instead.
Componentdate-picker · Helper textChangedCarbon: $label-01 — again the only field that does not use $helper-text-01Normalised to the shared field pattern.
Componentdate-picker · ShadowChangedCarbon: the style page publishes a raw '0 2px 6px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2)'; the shipped _flatpickr.scss calls @include box-shadow, which is '0 2px 6px $shadow' with $shadow at 30% alpha. The docs and the code disagree on the alpha, and only the docs are untokenised.A documentation defect rather than an implementation one — but it is the kind that propagates, because a designer redlining from the style page will specify 20% and get 30%.
Componentdate-picker · Range statesChangedCarbon: the calendar interactive-state table lists Hover, Focus, Disabled, Selected, In range, End range and Next month — there is no range-START rowThe gap is filled: range start uses the same treatment as Selected. Carbon's spellings 'In range' and 'End range' are kept.
Componentdate-picker · TodayChangedCarbon: $link-01 + a 4px dot. $link-01 is a v10 token name that appears exactly once across every page in the site repo — this row. Every other component uses $link-primary.Retokenised to link-primary.
Componenttable · Sticky headerAddedCarbon: no sticky-header design spec exists anywhere. Zero matches for sticky / frozen / pinned across all four data-table pages (usage, style, code, accessibility) — while DataTable.tsx declares stickyHeader?: boolean in three interfaces.A real gap in Carbon — the React implementation supports it, the design system never specified it.
Componentmodal · WidthsChangedCarbon: 'Modal widths are defined as percentages of the browser but will still align to columns on the 2x grid' — xs 24%, sm 36%, md 48%, lg 72% at 1584, with column spans (4/6/8/12 of 16) but no px values published anywherePercentage-of-viewport widths mean a dialog's measure changes with the browser, so body copy runs to 90+ characters on a wide monitor. Fixed max-widths with a viewport cap hold the measure constant, which is what dialog copy needs.
Componentmodal · ButtonsChangedCarbon: buttons span 50% of the modal each and bleed to its edges; three buttons are 25% eachFull-bleed 50% buttons make Cancel exactly as visually heavy as the primary action, which is the opposite of what a confirmation dialog should do.
Componentmodal · RadiusChangedCarbon: not published, and _modal.scss contains no border-radius declaration at allSee the radius scale.
Componentmodal · ScrimChangedCarbon: $overlay, black @60%, identical in all four themesTinted and lightened.
Componenttabs · RestChangedCarbon: border-bottom 2px $border-subtle ($tab-underline-color) — the same width as the selected state, only the colour changes1px at rest, 2px selected. Carbon's equal-width treatment means the resting underline carries as much visual weight as the selection indicator, so the selected tab has to rely on colour plus weight to separate itself. Halving the rest state lets the 2px selected rule read as an indicator rather than a recolour.
Componentnotification · BackgroundChangedCarbon: $notification-*-background-color component tokensPromoted to a core token — see support-*-subtle.
Componenttag · HeightsChangedCarbon: sm 18 / md 24 / lg 3218px is below the 20px minimum where a 12px label still has breathing room.
Componenttag · RadiusChangedCarbon: 16px at every size — one of only four radii Carbon publishes on a component page (Tag 16px, Content switcher 4px, Code snippet 2px, Popover 2px), against 22 component SCSS files that set one[encode 2026-08-20, E-09] The tag is the dot-chip: neutral bordered chip on layer-01, a 7px hue dot (grade 60 light / 40 dark) or icon in its place, and the WORD carrying the meaning. Tinted pills retired; hue modifier class names kept. The one element the appearance axes never vary.
Componenttag · TypeChangedCarbon: $label-01The T1 caps label (12/500/.4px). Chip text stays sentence-case via the component.
Componenttag · Group limitChangedCarbon (selectable tags in groups only): 'Keep groups of tags horizontally on one line when there are six tags or less.' and 'If the number of tags exceeds five lines of wrapping, consider using a different component for your use case, like a multi-select dropdown.' — a threshold and a soft 'consider', not a hard per-row cap.Applied to all tag variants rather than selectable groups only, and treated as a limit rather than a suggestion.
Componenttile · SurfaceChangedCarbon: $layer, and NO border row at all on the base tile — its colour table has exactly two rows, background and text. Clickable, selectable and expandable tiles do get $border-tile, but the style page labels it 'Border (feature flag)' and _tile.scss gates it behind enable-tile-contrast, so it is off by default.Border on all variants, unconditionally. A White-theme tile on layer-02 is otherwise invisible — which is presumably why the contrast feature flag exists at all. Strata takes the flagged behaviour as the default.
Componenttile · ElevationChangedCarbon: 'Tiles reside on the same plane as the page background layer and do not have elevation.' and 'Do not add a drop shadow to tiles and use them to reveal secondary information, actions, or notifications.' Carbon's own AI tile variant is an exception — it ships $ai-drop-shadow and $ai-inner-shadow.Carbon's no-shadow rule is right at rest and is kept. A hover lift on a clickable tile is a state change, not decoration, and it is the cheapest way to distinguish a clickable tile from a base one before the pointer commits.
Componenttile · RadiusChangedCarbon: not published; _tile.scss sets a radius only on the AI decorator variants, never on base, clickable or selectableSee the radius scale.

Worth getting right before this goes anywhere near a product.
